title: delurio binding (binding.yaml)
description: A binding ties a flow, or a navigation graph, to a running app for replay and recording, in delurio-graph/0 (SPEC.md §7). This schema describes its `ambient` answers, the calls the graph does not hold, answered in the app's place. The binding's other keys (`flow`, `nav`, `extends`, `root`, `apps`, `browser`, `data`, `signIn`, `accounts`, `scenarios`, `events`, `effects`, `states`, `nodes`, and a navigation binding's own) are SPEC.md §7's and are left open here. `check` does not read bindings.

schema.description: The format and its version. Every graph file starts with it.

kind.description: The kind of graph file. A binding is `binding`.

scenarios.description: The starts of the walks, by name (SPEC.md §7). A scenario may give `ambient` answers of its own, looked at before the binding's; its other keys are left open here.

ambient.description: The calls the graph does not hold, answered in the app's place: what a page asks its server for that no state's `call` names, such as the session, the person signed in (`/me`), feature flags, translations or an analytics endpoint. A call is what a page sends with `fetch` or `XMLHttpRequest`, or opens as a WebSocket or an `EventSource`; loading a document, a script, a style sheet, an image, a font or a media file is no call. A request that a state's `call` names is the graph's own, and is never answered here.

answers.description: The answers, in order: a request is answered by the first that matches it, the scenario's own before the binding's, and the binding's before those of a binding it `extends`.

others.description: What happens to a call that no state's `call` and no answer matches. `pass`, the default: it goes on to the app. `abort`: it fails as a failed network does, and the report names its address once, so a walk on a frontend served without its server reaches nothing the graph and the binding do not answer. A scenario's `others` takes the place of the binding's.

call.description: Which requests an answer is for: a URL glob, or `{ url, method }`, as a state's `call` is (SPEC.md §7).

method.description: The request's method; any method when it is left out.

networkError.description: The name of a network error, as a browser names it.

answer.description: One answer: `{ call, status, json, body, contentType, headers }`, what the server would have answered, or `{ call, abort }`, no answer at all. A string in `json`, `body` or `headers` may hold `{<source>.<path>}` values of the binding's data, read when the request is answered.

status.description: The answer's HTTP status; 200 when it is left out.

json.description: A value of any kind, sent as `application/json`.

contentType.description: The body's media type; `text/plain` when it is left out, and `application/json` for `json`.

headers.description: Headers the answer carries besides its content type.

abort.description: No answer, as a failed network gives: `true`, which is the error `failed`, or the error's name.

note.description: The author's own words. No tool reads them.

allOf.$comment: an answer sends one body: a JSON value or a text, not both
an answer that aborts sends nothing, so it has no status, body or headers
